title: Request-Scoped Semantic Enrichment Layer for Multisource Logs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a lightweight enrichment layer in the ingress pipeline that attaches deterministic, request-scoped semantic context to events from heterogeneous sources (edge proxies, runtime sidecars, batch replayers). Goals: 1) make downstream aggregation/alerting resilient to format drift by normalizing key semantic fields (service, endpoint, request_id, user_id hash, feature-flags), 2) ensure a stable correlation id surface for tracing and cross-log joins, 3) avoid inflating storage/ingest costs by selective field promotion and sampling, and 4) keep per-tenant privacy controls (PII redaction and hashed identifiers).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress enrichers annotate incoming events with deterministic request-scoped id (req_scoped_id) for >95% of successful HTTP flows
Normalized semantic fields (service, route, status_code, experiment) exist in Loki labels and Elastic mappings for new pipelines
End-to-end latency increase at the ingest proxy <= 4ms p95 under baseline load
Configurable rules allow customers to opt-out of identifier hashing and to apply tenant-specific redaction policies
Automated tests validate enrichment behavior for three common source formats: proxy-access-log, json-sidecar, batch-jsonl
updates: 2026-02-15 - Aisha: Ticket created after spike; initial prototype in sidecar accepted for PoC. Linked spec and sample datasets.

2026-02-18 - Marco: Spike results: deterministic req id derived from (trace_id || client_conn_id || timestamp) gives 99.2% coverage for HTTP flows; added privacy concerns for client_conn_id retention.

2026-02-22 - Eng sync: Decided enrichment runs as an independent phase before schema validation to avoid losing unrecognized fields. Trade-off: slightly higher memory usage vs fewer dropped semantics.
2026-02-26 - PR 4983 opened: basic enricher service + unit tests for jsonl and proxy logs. Requesting design review from Observability PM and Privacy lead.
2026-03-01 - Privacy review (Nora Kim): Approved hashing strategy for user identifiers; required opt-out flag for enterprise tenants and KMS-backed salt rotation schedule.
2026-03-03 - Load test: p95 enrichment latency 3.7ms added under 2k rps baseline; CPU cost ~6% on ingest-workers. Need to evaluate cost for Dedicated customers with small pools.

2026-03-05 - Marco: Implemented tenant-level policy config and a flag to disable enrichment for selected tenants. Next: add integration tests for Loki label mapping and Elastic ingestion mapping updates.
implementation_notes: Enricher will be implemented in Rust for the ingest-proxy hot path and as a Go fallback for sidecar. Use a feature-flagged pipeline to toggle heavy normalization rules. Sampling decisions (full vs metadata-only) propagate via the req_scoped_id so downstream replayers can materialize full events when requested.
tradeoffs_and_risks: - Deterministic id generation may collision in extreme NATed-client scenarios; mitigation: include a short HMAC with tenant salt. - Promoting many fields into Loki labels increases index cardinality; mitigation: only promote a curated list and support label-exclusion profiles per tenant. - Extra CPU on ingest nodes could require autoscale policy updates for bursty traffic.
qa_plan: Unit tests for field extraction and hashing rules; integration tests between ingest-proxy -> Loki -> Console dashboards; e2e test that replicates trace to logs join using test trace fixtures. Add chaos test that simulates malformed events and verifies enrichment is non-blocking.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag behind observability-pipeline-v3; 2) Canary on internal logging tenant for 48h; 3) Gradual rollout to 10% of customers with monitoring for p95 ingest latency, unique label cardinality, and error rates; 4) Full rollout with migration job to backfill req_scoped_id for recent 7 days if requested by customer.
notes_for_ops: Expose a /debug/metrics endpoint with enriched event counters and sample failcases. Add a runbook for salt rotation and tenant opt-out remediation steps. Alert if enrich_failure_rate > 0.5% for 15m or if label-cardinality growth > 30% week-over-week.
review_feedback: PM (Lydia): Keep label set minimal by default; surface promoted fields in Console so teams can request additions.
Design (Ravi): Provide sample log lines and a mapping UI in Console for custom field-to-label mappings.
Security (Nora): Require KMS-backed salts; prohibit storing raw user identifiers in enriched output unless tenant flagged and audited.
